title: 8.7 A Dual VDD-Temperature Sensor Employing Sensor Fusion with 2.4°C, 9mV (±3σ) Inaccuracy in 65nm CMOS
problem: Heterogeneous 3D chiplet systems face acute thermal and power delivery challenges: thermal hotspots from high power density and workload-dependent supply voltage (VDD) gradients require fine-grained spatiotemporal monitoring via temperature and VDD sensors, but achieving high accuracy without external references is difficult.
motivation: Run-time thermal and power management in chiplets demands system-wide networks of compact, low-latency, accurate temperature and VDD sensors; measuring both parameters simultaneously with sensor fusion improves coverage with minimal overhead.
method: Dual-sensor design combining temperature and VDD measurement via sensor fusion in 65nm CMOS; achieves 2.4°C and 9mV (±3σ) inaccuracy without external references, operating reliably despite VDD scaling and noise across different SoC domains.
key_novelty: First demonstrated sensor fusion approach combining temperature and VDD sensing in single compact IP, enabling simultaneous thermal and power-delivery monitoring without external calibration—critical for 3D chiplet thermal/power management.
contributions: Dual temperature and VDD sensor with integrated sensor fusion
9 mV VDD accuracy (±3σ) robust to supply noise and scaling
Compact integration in 65nm CMOS suitable for distributed chiplet networks

metrics.other: No external references, robust to VDD noise/scaling, fine spatiotemporal resolution

baselines: Prior separate temperature and VDD sensors (refs 1), prior integrated approaches without fusion
limitations: Power consumption, latency, and dynamic responsiveness during workload transitions not specified; comparison with state-of-the-art monitoring solutions not provided.
primary_theme: Fused temperature and VDD sensor for chiplet thermal/power management
